Additive: no boundary tool contract or param schema changed and no existing skill was edited, so serverInfo.version stays '0.5.0' and boundary_compat is unchanged ('>=0.5.0 <0.6.0') - a patch bump, not a minor. 0.6.3 -> 0.6.4 (fix): four duty-mapping defects in the Article 50 scanner, all found by adversarial review with crafted fixtures and independently reproduced. Three of the four made the tool report a CLEAN directory on material that was not clean, which is the failure mode that matters most for a scanner the skill recommends as a delivery gate. (1): scan() walked the disk and never reconciled the declaration's asset keys against what it found, so a declared asset missing from disk vanished from the report entirely -- a typo, a rename or a not-yet-delivered path discharged every 50(2) and 50(4) duty attached to it and the tool exited 0. Reconciliation now runs in both directions: an unmatched declaration key raises the new high-severity declared-asset-not-found gap (distinguishing 'no file there' from 'present but not a scanned extension'), and unmatched entries feed the production-level 50(4) check so a missing deep fake can no longer clear the production disclosure gap. (2): the 50(4) second-subparagraph rule was inverted -- it tested only public_interest_text against editorial_responsibility, never consulted disclosure_statement, and so raised a high-severity gap on productions that HAD disclosed while clearing on an editorial owner named with no evidence anyone reviewed the text. The statute makes disclosure the duty and human review PLUS editorial responsibility the two-limbed exception that lifts it, and the check now follows that structure: disclosure clears it, editorial_responsibility alone does not. This makes the per-asset human_review field load-bearing (it was parsed and never read by any rule) and adds production.human_review as its production-level counterpart. The gap id is renamed public-interest-text-unreviewed -> public-interest-text-undisclosed, because it now fires on the absence of disclosure rather than the absence of review; the old id never described the condition it actually tested. (3): disclosure_statement was tested with bare truthiness, so a whitespace-only value -- the artifact of a form writing a space where it meant to omit the key -- read as a present disclosure and cleared every 50(4) check, while its empty-string sibling correctly raised gaps. Disclosure text is now stripped before it is tested everywhere it is tested. (4) (reporting accuracy, not gating): production.artistic_work was documented in DECLARATION.md but read only from the merged defaults/asset entry, so an asset covered by a production-level declaration was reported as artistic_work false. It is now inherited when the asset does not override it, deliberately at the point of use rather than in _declared_for, so a production-level field cannot make an asset with no entry of its own look declared. SKILL.md documents the two new gap ids and DECLARATION.md the public_interest_text rule, the stripped-text behavior, the artistic_work precedence and the both-directions reconciliation. The scope-limits text printed in every report is unchanged and still accurate. Regression tests: tests/test_article50_scan.py, 25 cases, one named class per issue. Skill content only: no boundary tool contract or param schema changed, so serverInfo.version stays '0.5.0' and boundary_compat is unchanged ('>=0.5.0 <0.6.0') -- a patch bump, not a minor. Three of the four fixes were widened after a second adversarial pass reproduced adjacent cases the issues did not name. also covers declaration keys that miss on CASE only (a delivered SH040_Likeness.PNG against a declared sh040_likeness.png) -- the realistic form of the defect, where the file WAS delivered and nothing connects it to its declaration, so the asset is scanned as though undeclared. Keys match exactly, case included; the gap names the delivered file so the fix is one line, but the scan will not match them for you, because on a case-sensitive filesystem two files can differ only in capitals and guessing would attach a deep-fake duty to the wrong asset. This also required scan() to reconcile against the paths the walk actually saw rather than asking Path.is_file, which answers differently on a case-insensitive volume and made the report platform-dependent (a case-missed .png read as 'present under an unassessed extension' on macOS and as 'absent' on Linux). also covers NON-STRING disclosure values: true, a nonzero number, {} and [] cleared the 50(4) axis through the same bare truthiness as whitespace. These fields are defined as the words a person is shown, so they now require a non-empty string once stripped -- a bare true is a checkbox, not a sentence.'s exemption test is conjunctive as before, and the review limb is now scoped to TEXT (whether an image was reviewed says nothing about whether the published article was read by a person) with an explicit human_review:false on any declared text decisive over a positive record elsewhere: a publication containing AI text the operator states nobody reviewed is not one the exemption reaches. Test count 25 -> 34. 0.6.4 -> 0.6.5 (patch, correctness): scopes the Article 50(4) public-interest review limb so a defaults.human_review flag only counts where it actually reaches a declared text asset; previously an image-only production with that default cleared the text disclosure duty and reported no gap ( follow-up). Test count 34 -> 37. 0.6.6 (correctness): Article 50 marking detection is now grounded in parsed containers and read sidecars. The whole-file substring fallback that credited any file containing the text c2pa.claim is gone, JPEG APP11 matching requires the C2PA type UUID, sidecars are matched to their own asset and their contents read, zero-length manifests no longer count as present, and the head-plus-tail read no longer manufactures marker bytes across the seam. JUMBF boxes with a zero LBox (spec-legal, running to the end of the enclosing container) are accepted. 0.6.7 (correctness): text metadata is parsed rather than proximity-searched. The IPTC digital source type is read as the property's own value, generator fingerprints are anchored instead of matched anywhere in free text, and generation-parameter blocks are recognized by shape. Caption-carrying surfaces need two sampler-setting keys; EXIF UserComment needs one. PNG generator keys split by whether the name is AI-exclusive: sd-metadata and invokeai_metadata count on the name, while parameters, prompt and workflow require a real generation record, so an org chart whose exporter wrote a workflow caption is no longer read as AI output. 0.6.8 (correctness): assessment now asks what a marking says, not merely whether one is present, so a credential asserting a camera capture no longer discharges the Article 50(2) duty. A declaration and the metadata are checked against each other in both directions, the four declared boolean fields raise declaration-field-malformed when the value is not a real boolean at the production level as well as per asset, a declaration of the wrong shape reports an error rather than reading as gaps found, Article 50(4) reaches text assets on the subparagraph that actually applies, and a contradiction message names the artifact that carries the conflicting claim. 0.6.9 (correctness): scan coverage now tells the truth about itself. Anything the scanner could not read, including a broken symlink, a symlink loop, and a symlink standing where a media file appears to be, raises asset-unreadable, reaches the gap list a person reads, and sets the exit code, so silence means examined rather than blocked. A declaration path given relative to the working directory no longer scans the declaration itself as an asset, --max-bytes below 1 is rejected rather than claiming whole-file coverage, a non-regular file with a media extension no longer hangs the scan, and a write failure on any output path, the default output stream included, exits 2 rather than reading as gaps found. 0.7.0 (correctness): the production block's operator and role are read the way the wording fields are, so a value that is only whitespace counts as absent and raises operator-unnamed or role-unstated rather than passing as a declaration. A role outside the documented vocabulary of provider, deployer and both raises role-unrecognized and quotes what was written, since a misspelling answers the question no better than a blank while leaving the gap list silent. Case and surrounding space are tolerated. The field still does not select which checks run, and DECLARATION.md now says so plainly. This follows the report's existing convention for operator-declared text: presented as a declaration, not a finding, the same as the per-asset declared block already carries model and disclosure -- nothing here is validated, exactly as DECLARATION.md's closing paragraph already stated. (1) A leading dot removed a file from the scan before the extension test SKILL.md says decides scope ever ran: walk_assets pruned any dot-prefixed directory (never descended) and any dot-prefixed file (never examined), so a delivered .hero_final.jpg produced no record anywhere in the report -- not an asset, not an unreadable, not a gap -- and a DECLARED one was reported as declared-asset-not-found, 'no file was found at it', which is false about a file that is present, readable and genuinely signed. (2) production.title, operator and role reached the Markdown gap list unsanitised, so the party whose claims the scan exists to cross-check could forge or hide the tool's own verdict: a newline plus a fabricated '## Gaps / No gaps recorded' block and a bare '<!--' made every CommonMark renderer swallow the real high-severity gap and the whole limits section as comment text (verified against the reference commonmark implementation, the grammar GitHub renders), a role could forge a '### High (0)' header under the real one, and raw ANSI escapes cleared the terminal of anyone who cat-ed the report over the real findings. Every value spliced into the gap list -- asset paths and the quoted role included -- is now stripped of control and format characters, and the operator-authored title and operator are shown as code spans. A rendering rule, not a rewrite: the JSON report still carries all three character for character. (3) A lone UTF-16 surrogate in one of those fields (valid JSON per RFC 8259 sec. 8.2, unencodable in UTF-8) raised UnicodeEncodeError, a ValueError rather than an OSError, so it escaped the write guard whose own comment says an undelivered artifact is exit 2 -- and the tool exited 1 with a traceback on every documented output path, which a CI gate reads as 'gaps found' in a report that was never written. The guard now catches UnicodeError alongside OSError. (4) A declaration holding one invalid UTF-8 byte crashed the whole scan before any output existed, bypassing the declaration-unparsable degradation path built for exactly this condition; read_text's UnicodeDecodeError is caught the same way a JSON syntax error already was, so the scan runs against file metadata alone and reports honestly that the declaration was ignored. (5) The Article 50(4) second-subparagraph check consulted only production.disclosure_statement and never the per-asset disclosure the same file already reads for the deep-fake limb, so an operator who wrote the disclosure on the one declared public-interest text asset was told they had not disclosed. Disclosure now clears the duty at either level; every declared text must carry one, because disclosing one article says nothing about the next, and a production declaring the duty with no text entry still raises the gap. SKILL.md and DECLARATION.md state the rendering rule, the UTF-8 declaration path and the two-level disclosure. Regression tests: tests/test_article50_scan.py, 347 -> 368 cases. Skill content only: no boundary tool contract or param schema changed, so serverInfo.version stays '0.5.0' and boundary_compat is unchanged ('>=0.5.0 <0.6.0') -- a patch bump, not a minor. 0.7.2 -> 0.7.3 (correctness, docs): the two launch-gate findings the 0.7.2 pass left open, both of them a published promise the code did not keep. The prune is now routed out of the walk the way an unlistable directory already is, and the gap names the directory that withheld the path, tells the operator the file was not examined and not judged, and offers the repairs that exist: move it out, or scan that directory as its own root. The entry stays in the unmatched set, so's rule that a declared deep fake cannot be cleared by a file the scan never read holds here too. (2) A failed write on the bare stdout path exited 120, not the documented 2. stdout to a pipe is block-buffered, so for a report small enough to fit the buffer the write syscall happened when the interpreter flushed at exit -- outside main()'s guard -- and the BrokenPipeError there printed "Exception ignored" and replaced the exit code with Python's 120, which is neither the 2 the docs promise nor a code a CI gate recognises. The flush now happens inside the guard and stdout is redirected to the null device once a write to it has failed, so the interpreter's last flush cannot overwrite the classification. The existing test could not see this: its gap list deliberately exceeds the pipe buffer, which forces the flush inside the guard. The exit-code promise itself is narrowed to what a writer can know. README.md, SKILL.md and the module docstring said a gap list piped into a consumer that exits early "is a report that never arrived, so it exits 2"; a report that fits the kernel pipe buffer is accepted by write() before the reader closes, and nothing afterwards tells the writer it went unread. Polling the descriptor for POLLHUP was considered and rejected: a timing-dependent exit code is worse for a gate than an under-reported one. All three surfaces now promise exit 2 for a write that fails, a broken pipe included, on every output path, and SKILL.md states the residue plainly -- a 2 cannot tell you a consumer read the report; write to a file if the gate depends on that. README.md's exit-code sentence, which documented only 0 and 1 while SKILL.md and --help documented all three, now names 2 as the code that must not be read as "gaps found", and "That is the whole setup." is cut, the same editorial call already made against the identical sentence in the launch post. Article 50(2)'s own exception existed nowhere in the tool. With no time_scale the numbers are unchanged. `studio emit publish_clip` refuses, like `clips publish-clip`, when CLIP names a clip on stages.clips.items and CLIP_NAME is not the verified `clips build` title; a CLIP not on the manifest is not gated. `clips transfer` takes the poses.py options directly: `--g <name>` or `--g-from <Clip>` (reads that clip's recorded g from its poses doc and forces it; refused if that clip has no doc or no g; the two are mutually exclusive), `--no-root`, `--root-ref first|bind`, and `--trim START:END` (seconds of the source clip). poses.py gains `--trim=START:END`: it keeps that frame range, re-based to start at 0, before the root reference, axis scoring and trajectories, so clip_seconds is the trimmed length; it refuses a range past the clip's end or one that keeps fewer than two frames, and a malformed range is refused before Blender runs. The item records g, g_forced, g_from, root_motion, root_ref and trim, and the poses doc records trim. `clips transfer` of the clip `clips impact` last measured drops stages.clips.attackImpactDelaySecs, attackImpactRawSecs and attackImpactClip (with a note to re-run `clips impact`), and `clips build` refuses when the recorded raw impact time is past the clip's clip_seconds. `studio emit publish_clip` now also refuses a CLIP that is not on stages.clips.items (or no CLIP at all) unless --param UNVERIFIED_OK=<reason> is passed; the reason is written to the manifest notes and is not rendered into the step. UNVERIFIED_OK does not bypass the check for a clip that is on the manifest. 0.10.14 -> 0.10.15 (patch): clip root motion is calibrated. poses.py scales root motion by k, now the leg-chain ratio (hip joint -> knee -> ankle, both sides) between rest.json and the clip's bind, recorded as k and k_source in the poses doc and k on the clip item; it was the rig height over the clip's bone-head span measured after the rename/merge, which on a library skeleton is about hips-to-skull and made root motion 1.37x too large. Pose and rest matrices are reduced to their rotation part, so a bone scale the clip keys no longer produces non-unit quaternions. `--rig-height` is still accepted and only reported. `clips transfer --root-y ground` (poses.py --root-y=ground --rig-mesh=<glb>) is a new opt-in vertical root mode: each frame's vertical offset puts the rig's lowest skinned vertex back on its rest level, with the horizontal still following --root-ref; it skins stages.rig.artifact_glb unless --rig-mesh names another glb, fits it to rest.json by a similarity and refuses a bone-origin miss over 1% of the mesh height, and refuses --no-root. The item and poses doc record root_y (hips, the default, or ground) and the fit (ground). A clip transferred before 0.10.15 keeps its old root motion until it is re-transferred and rebuilt (`clips transfer`, then `clips build`); its rotations change only where the source keyed a bone scale. k also scales the truth ranges the empirical axis-map pick scores against, so a clip re-transferred without --g may pick a different map than it did before 0.10.15 (the reference walk kept its pick; its scores moved from 18.17 vs 20.06 to 3.80 vs 4.98): compare the `g` the transfer records with the old one, and pin it with `--g <name>` or `--g-from <Clip>`. 0.10.15 -> 0.10.16 (breaking, runner CLI): a title declares its own clip keys beside the catalog's. Additive: `clips declare --clip <key> --loop true|false --priority Idle|Movement|Action [--description <motion>]` records stages.clips.declared.<key> = {loop, priority, description}; the key is letters and digits starting with a letter, and a catalog clip's name (in any case) or a key that differs from a declared key or a key on stages.clips.items only in case is refused. The steps that create a clip (`clips transfer`, `clips emit motion`, `clips ingest motion`) take a catalog clip or a declared key; a declared key takes its loop and priority from the declaration, `clips emit motion` asks for its description and refuses a key declared without one (`clips ingest motion` does not: it records the file the caller has, with no prompt), and `clips transfer --source catalog` on a declared key is refused (it has no catalog candidates: use `clips ingest motion`, then `--source generated`). The steps that act on a clip (`clips build`, `build-kfs`, `publish-clip`, `bench`, `impact`, `registered`, and `bind --ids`) take any key on stages.clips.items, so an item a title's own transfer wrote needs no declaration. --clip no longer carries argparse choices: it is checked after the manifest loads, and an unknown key is refused by name, listing the valid keys. The published title is <Name><Key>_v<N> with the key's first letter upper-cased (a catalog clip's title is unchanged). `clips impact` keeps one impact clip (attackImpactClip) whichever key it measures. New in clips.py: declare, declared, known_key, item_key, clip_props, description_of, catalog_candidate, CLIP_KEY_RE, ARCHIVE_SOURCES. Breaking: `clips bind` refuses, before any payload, a clip whose item source is none of generated, rig-bundled, mixamo-archive or quaternius unless the item carries source_media_id (the Genvid row of the file it was transferred from), which bind cites in input_media_ids and generation.params.source_record; a title whose own transfer writes clip items records that id on the item before `clips bind`, and an existing manifest whose items carry another source (for example "meshy-library" or "authored") needs source_media_id on each such item before it is bound again. Breaking: UNVERIFIED_OK is removed: `studio emit publish_clip` refuses a CLIP not on stages.clips.items with no bypass, and refuses any call that passes UNVERIFIED_OK (studio.require_verified takes no unverified_ok argument); declare the title's key and build it as an item instead. Breaking: `clips bind` registers each clip under the title `clips build` recorded for it (items.<Clip>.kfs_name), so clips at different versions bind in one call; --version now defaults to none, and a --version/--name that gives another title for a built clip is refused before any payload (a clip with no build record is refused unless --version is passed, with --name when the title's prefix is not the manifest's name: bind no longer defaults to version 1). `clips transfer --g-from <key>` (and clips.recorded_g) refuses a key with no transferred item on stages.clips.items instead of reading <out_dir>/clips/<key>.poses.json.
